site.name: brewlog-mobile
site.summary: brewlog-mobile Fictional coffee-brewing journal "Brewlog" iOS-style mobile fixture. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - 390 × 844 phone frame with chrome bezel, notch, status bar, home indicator - Bottom 4-tab bar: Today / Add / Stats / Beans - Edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px) Screens | `data-screen` | Highlights |

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the brewlog-mobile SPA, focusing on tab navigation, the brew logging form, and data visualization screens.
run_plan.summary: The run will proceed by systematically verifying each of the four main bottom navigation tabs: Today, Add, Stats, and Beans. It will thoroughly test the form inputs in the 'Log a brew' view and validate the display of data visualizations in the 'Stats' view, while keeping an eye on mobile layout constraints and tap target sizes.
assumptions: The site operates as a Single Page Application (SPA) within index.html, using DOM manipulation or CSS to switch between the Today, Add, Stats, and Beans screens.
The 29 inputs found in the prescan belong primarily to the 'Log a brew' form.
The desktop viewport will likely render the mobile frame centered on the screen, while the mobile viewport will test edge-to-edge rendering.
risk_hotspots: Tap target size of the '+ Log' button in the header (flagged as 70x31px).
Form validation and keyboard usability for the large number of inputs (29) on the 'Log a brew' screen.
Responsiveness and readability of data visualizations (Score over time, Method mix) on small screens.
Bottom navigation bar overlapping with actual mobile home indicators or content.

phases.title: Today View & Navigation Initialization
phases.objective: Verify the default 'Today' screen, scroll through existing brew entries, and ensure bottom tabs are visible and functional.
key_checks: Check visibility of 'TODAY' and 'YESTERDAY' brew entries.
Verify that the bottom navigation bar (Today, Add, Stats, Beans) is fixed at the bottom.
Click the '+ Log' button in the header to ensure it routes to the Add screen, then return to 'Today'.
exit_criteria: Scroll behavior on the 'Today' screen is confirmed, and basic routing via the header button works.

phases.title: Log a Brew Form
phases.objective: Thoroughly exercise the 'Add' screen form fields and attempt a submission.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Add' via the bottom navigation.
Interact with various input types (text, numbers, sliders/toggles if present) for beans, grind, dose, yield, time, and score.
Test form validation by submitting empty or invalid data.
Submit a valid entry and check if the UI provides feedback or redirects back to 'Today' with the new entry.
exit_criteria: Form validation logic is triggered and recorded, and a successful (or mocked) submission flow is completed.

phases.title: Stats & Data Visualization
phases.objective: Explore the 'Stats' tab to evaluate the rendering and readability of charts and metrics.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Stats' via the bottom navigation.
Check the presence and layout of 'Score over time', 'Method mix', and 'Top tasting notes' headings.
Verify that charts or graphs are completely visible without horizontal scrolling overflow on mobile.
exit_criteria: All visualization sections in the Stats view have been inspected for layout issues.

phases.title: Beans Database & State Persistence
phases.objective: Verify the 'Beans' tab and ensure application state is stable across tab switching.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Beans' via the bottom navigation and inspect the list/grid of beans.
Switch rapidly back and forth between 'Today', 'Stats', and 'Beans' to ensure the UI does not glitch or lose state.
exit_criteria: The Beans view is fully loaded and tab switching behaves predictably.

coverage_targets.pages: Explore all SPA 'screens' (Today, Add, Stats, Beans) within index.html.
coverage_targets.features: Fill out and submit the brew logging form; view all data charts.
coverage_targets.mobile: Strictly evaluate layout clipping, tap target sizes, and scrolling physics in the mobile viewport.

notes: Since this is a fixture simulating a mobile environment, pay special attention to how it renders on the desktop viewport (e.g., does it break out of its container, or is it strictly constrained?).
